title: Enable two-phase checking in sequential mode when --local-partial-types is set
author: ilevkivskyi
body_preview: Right now there may be minor inconsistencies between sequential and parallel mode, because the latter uses two-phase checking (interfaces, then implementations). We should (gradually) switch sequential mode to the two-phase checking as well.

title: Use log files for parallel workers stdout/stderr
author: ilevkivskyi
body_preview: Right now parallel workers use stdout/stderr for tracing/logging, and for error reporting in case of a crash. We may want to instead use log files (one per worker), similar to daemon. I am however not 100% sure this is better.  cc @JukkaL

title: Support parallel checking in fine grained mode
author: ilevkivskyi
body_preview: This includes at least two things: * Make sure all fine-grained dependencies are written when using `--cache-fine-grained` on a regular run * Speed up the daemon cold start by running it with multiple workers that would write the initial cache  cc @JukkaL

title: Add dedicated tests for parallel mode
author: ilevkivskyi
body_preview: We should add some dedicated unit tests for parallel mode to check various workers scheduling logic, for example massively parallel workload, single SCC workload etc.

title: Suport various reports in parallel mode
author: ilevkivskyi
body_preview: Various reports, like type coverage/type precision reports are nor supported in parallel mode. It would be great to support this. The non-trivial part is that we write to the same file deep in the reporters logic. Instead workers should either write per-file reports that will be aggregated by the coordinator, or send them back to the coordinator over IPC (which may require more code changes).

body_preview: I think this is very much needed PEP, and using mypy for reference implementation is a good idea because mypy actually already (mostly) supports this under the hood. title: `heapq.merge`, `heapq.nlargest` and `heapq.nsmallest` are typed inadequately
author: jonathandung
body_preview: The current annotations for the above functions mean that their `key` arguments can be omitted for iterables of objects that do not implement the rich comparison operators without triggering a type checker diagnostic, whereas that will likely fail with `TypeError` at runtime. They should be overloaded accordingly.

title: `_heapq.heapify` and `_heapq.heapify_max` do not required type variables to annotate
author: jonathandung
body_preview: In the signatures of both `_heapq.heapify` and `_heapq.heapify_max`, the `_T` type variable, an alias to `_typeshed.SupportsRichComparisonT`, can be replaced with `_typeshed.SupportsRichComparison` because they are used only once.
